title: EEF Evidence Edit: Intelligent Tutoring, Maths Research, and Responsive Teaching rogramme
author: Education Endowment Foundation
summary: This edition of the EEF’s Evidence Edit newsletter reports findings from four new independent evaluations on maths, STEM teaching, and professional development. The headline result: an NFER evaluation of Maths-Whizz across 63 primary schools found pupils made the equivalent of one additional month’s progress on average, and two additional months for pupils eligible for free school meals—earning the programme an EEF “Promising” designation with a four-padlock security rating. The newsletter frames intelligent tutoring (personalised pathways, adaptive support, real-time feedback) as a promising route to better maths outcomes, alongside evaluations of Aspire to STEM, One Step Ahead, The 5 Rs, and Thinking Mathematically. It also features EEF CEO Becky Francis on tackling disadvantage and a guest blog on responsive teaching for pupils with SEND.
points: Maths-Whizz was designated an EEF Promising Programme after an NFER evaluation across 63 primary schools showed one additional month’s maths progress on average.
Pupils eligible for free school meals gained the equivalent of two additional months’ progress—a notable signal for narrowing the disadvantage gap.

Intelligent tutoring—personalised pathways, adaptive support, and real-time feedback—is framed as having genuine potential to improve maths outcomes, with small positive effects on confidence and enjoyment.
Four evaluations in total (Aspire to STEM, One Step Ahead, The 5 Rs, Thinking Mathematically) add to the evidence base for maths and STEM teaching.
A guest blog argues responsive teaching—checking understanding and adapting in the moment—helps pupils with SEND access and succeed with learning.
quotes: An independent evaluation by NFER across 63 primary schools found that pupils using Maths-Whizz made the equivalent of one additional month's progress in maths, on average.
Pupils eligible for free school meals made the equivalent of two additional months' progress.
The findings suggest that intelligent tutoring, including personalised learning pathways, adaptive support and real-time feedback, has the potential to improve maths outcomes
With a four-padlock security rating, Maths-Whizz has now been designated an EEF Promising Programme.
Even the best-planned lessons can't predict exactly how every pupil will respond to new learning.
Rather than relying on assumptions, teachers can use evidence gathered during lessons to make informed adaptations that support all pupils.
